problems.rationale: The acceptance criterion is a pre-registered GBIF tournament on a defined archipelago list, fitting the power law, METE and at least two alternatives under one sampling correction, and the workable route is coverage-standardized richness for plants, land birds and snails on the six named island groups. The shared blocker is that small-island GBIF coverage often misses the 0.95 target, especially for snails, and METE needs abundances that occurrences only approximate, so the GBIF approaches fail together rather than as independent draws. A logseries or Coleman null can finish and still not meet that criterion, which is why the 30-day problem probability sits below those computations' completion-times-settlement products. Released Triantis raw S–A tables with standard errors, or GIFT group identifiers that actually cluster islands, would move the year number up.

approaches.note: I put completion above the proposer's hard band because logging the coverage-failure signature still counts, but snail bias and abundance proxies often leave the three-way rule inconclusive.
The Coleman grid is a finite computation, yet SAD parameters that are not in the compilations can be tuned so the null matches any observed z.
Random-effects τ is computable from published z values, but missing raw curves and fewer than 20 abundance datasets make both τ and the METE collapse easy to leave uninterpretable.
Thirty archipelagos with spatially blocked ELPD is a stricter GBIF pipeline than the six-group test, and the slice already flags unreliable polygons and coverage below 0.5.
No harmonized public collection of nested surveys is named in the slice, so the likely logged outcome is that fewer than 30 series retain six scales.
GIFT checklists are a concrete download, but the test stops if group identifiers are missing and a METE-versus-power split on AIC versus residual is defined as not a win.
Once a pooled z is frozen, placing it inside or outside a logseries placement interval is a small simulation whose either outcome answers the sampling question.
Encoding the Harte MaxEnt area curve and its local exponent in Lean is real analysis, not a routine lemma, but a no-sorry proof or a constant-slope counterexample would settle the model claim.

problems.rationale: The route that matches the acceptance text is a shareholder-quorum census of PBDB orders and families against a duration-conditioned birth–death null, and the Paleobiology Database is already wired into the organisms layer. The shared blocker is that conditioned random walks are themselves hat-shaped and accepted names are not monophyly, so several SQS scripts can finish and still not separate a biological hat from the null or from the pull of the recent. A sampling-intensity interval can exonerate or indict the collection curve without supplying the required monophyly filter, so I do not treat that computation's product as a lower bound on the problem. An Open Tree subset that still leaves dozens of families, and a quorum sweep from 0.4 to 0.7 that does not flip the call, would move me.

approaches.note: SQS plus an MBL null on families with at least 50 occurrences is a standard PBDB job, but conditioning on duration and terminal diversity can make the null itself hat-shaped and leave no detectable excess.
Hundreds of PyRate runs, each hours to days, will not fit in 30 days of agent time, and preservation trends often leave the age slope of net diversification spanning zero.
Birth–death simulations with a pull-of-the-recent sampler are tractable, but the Linnaean divergence threshold is arbitrary and can make the artifact share any size the author wants.
A marine-only SQS census at quorum 0.6 is finishable, yet the 75 percent universality bar is likely to reverse between quorums 0.4 and 0.7, which the approach itself treats as inconclusive.
State-space birth–death recovery on 50 clades needs monophyly labels the slice says are unreliable, and the calibration step can confuse hats with sampling heterogeneity.

I rate completion above the hard label because a finished SQS script either clears the 0.5 excess bar or logs a null or recent-stage flip, both of which answer the hat question, even without monophyly.
The global marine collection curve is one frozen PBDB query, and whether the empirical hat fraction sits in its central 95 percent is a direct artifact call.
AIC on stage-to-stage SQS changes is lighter than PyRate, but diversity-dependent extinction can lose while curves still look hat-shaped, which settles only the Red Queen piece.

problems.rationale: Acceptance requires MorphoEval measurements of Raup's W, D and T, then developmental, functional and phylogenetic occupancy models scored on held-out taxa, plus an empty-region map. The realistic route is the 30-species floor on open MorphoSource meshes, not a 500- or 1000-shell corpus, because the slice says scan coverage is uneven and ammonoids are mostly 2D. A planispiral non-intersection proof or a geometric grid can finish without naming which mechanism wins, and a tie with a phylogenetic Gaussian process is the stated falsifier that leaves the question open, so those products are not lower bounds on the problem. Thirty families with wall meshes and an Open Tree subtree would move the year figure; public scans will not grow just because agents keep working.

approaches.note: Logging fewer than about 200 quality-filtered species counts as completion, and that underpowered stop is the likely outcome relative to the 500-species target.
I put this below the tractable band because a 10^4-shell finite-element compression grid exceeds a simulation preview, and the Pareto front can be so wide that it predicts no empty region.

The D = 1/W touching law is a plausible Lean target, but the elliptical and helicospiral generalizations plus a Moulton–Goriely reachability density are a second project the growth-rule family may leave uninformative.
One thousand consistently oriented meshes and an ICC above 0.9 against manual measurements are not supported by the open scan coverage described in the slice.
A million-point W–D–T lattice with certified stress is a large mechanics run, and species-specific material properties and load cases are missing, so feasible empty regions are the expected miss.
Disjointness of two successive circular generating curves is a narrow algebraic statement, and a no-sorry equivalence would settle that boundary without saying why real shells are absent.
The 30-species floor is the only occupancy tournament that matches public meshes, and falling short or failing to beat the phylogenetic process is defined as leaving the question open.
Gridding self-intersection is cheap once the circle test exists, but a large non-intersecting empty region is the historically expected result and only rules geometry out.

problems.rationale: Both acceptance pieces are desk work: compare N = T_elongation / T_clock with vertebral counts for every species that already has a published clock and elongation duration, and rank unmeasured species by how much a clock measurement would shrink uncertainty. The blocker is the slice's own fact that those durations exist for only a handful of species, seeded by Gomez et al. 2008, and the swarm has no time-lapse lab, so a 6- or 15-species support bar is expected to be underpowered even when the comparison is logged. The FishBase ranking can finish without that comparative test clearing its tolerance, which is why the 30-day problem probability stays below that ranking's product. Six species with clock and count taken from different papers would move me; new imaging would, and is outside this swarm.

approaches.note: I rate completion slightly above the hard band because the Gomez species plus in vitro PSM papers are a small literature table, but n under 4 or mismatched temperatures leaves the 15 percent rule unsettled.

A closed-form elasticity lemma is plausible in Lean, but PSM time courses exist as figures, and leave-one-out error above 30 percent is a real miss if termination is Hox timing rather than PSM depletion.
Matched clock-temperature series and rearing-temperature vertebral counts in the same species are described as rare, so the Arrhenius comparison is likely to stay cross-species and indirect.
Requiring 15 species across five classes will hit the stated failure of fewer than 10 direct measurements, which completes the log and does not answer the mechanism.

A sensitivity map over period, elongation and arrest-front speed can be simulated from published time courses, but period and elongation are often structurally nonidentifiable, which the approach treats as a failed discrimination.
The 25 percent ratio test on independently published counts is small enough to run, and the proposer correctly expects the underpowered floor below six species.
FishBase vertebral counts and an Open Tree covariance are public comparative data, and the ranked variance-reduction list is itself the decisive artifact even if tetrapods are only partly covered.
Freezing a zebrafish delayed-coupling oscillator and inserting published chick, mouse and snake periods is a clear three-species pass or fail, if the published speeds are usable without refitting.

problems.rationale: DRIVE and HRF gold-standard segmentations plus an open vascular model repository are enough to estimate a junction exponent, and that is the part of the acceptance test the swarm can actually run. The criterion also wants a third class, including xylem, and the McCulloh 2003 radii may not be numeric tables, while 2D retinal radii can leave an interval wide enough to contain both 3 and 7/3. Lean derivations of the Poiseuille-plus-volume cost can finish at high settlement and still say nothing about tissues, so their products are not a floor under the problem. A transcribed branch-point file for xylem, or a synthetic calibration that shows which pixel diameter separates 3 from 7/3, would move me.

approaches.note: DRIVE, HRF, VesSAP and transcribed tables can yield per-tissue intervals, but the approach's own failure is that retinal noise wider than ±0.5 cannot separate 3 from 7/3.
Strict convexity of the cubic cost and the 7/3 turbulent variant are calculus theorems Mathlib can host, and a compiled module would settle the derivation rather than the measurements.
Synthetic trees with a fundus and a light-sheet forward model are buildable, but if the synthetic contrast statistics do not match real images the calibration does not transfer.
Five hundred bifurcations in three modalities including calibrated 3D trees is harder than retina alone, and the slice says quality-controlled open vascular trees are what is missing.
A generalized exponent for resistance proportional to r to the minus k is the same convex-cost proof as the cubic law, with a slightly wider theorem and the same Mathlib friction.
Proving r cubed proportional to Q and isolating the single (a, b) pair that yields 7/3 is a compact Lean target that either pins the turbulent alternative or shows the cost family does not.
DRIVE, HRF and the Vascular Model Repository are named open sources, but a pooled interval that contains both 3 and 7/3 is the pre-registered unresolved outcome.
The xylem arm stops if the 2003 tables cannot be transcribed without guessing, and a retinal slope of exponent on log radius can easily include zero.

problems.rationale: This is the slice's most executable problem: INDRA CoGEx and Gene Ontology can run a permutation matched on set size, annotation count and degree for GO:0009653 versus GO:0007611, with ion-channel and gap-junction subsets as primary endpoints, which is the acceptance text. The existing levin-2022-tame-19 refutation did not control pleiotropy, so the new test is not already done, but the same annotation fashion can collapse strata or confine a hit to IEA evidence, and the overlap approaches share that bias rather than failing independently. An odds ratio that clears 2 with permutation p below 0.01 on the experimental-evidence run, and the same sign on the two bioelectric subsets, would meet the criterion inside 30 days. Pre-2015 assignment dates, if the download actually contains them, and an IMPC morphology-versus-behaviour odds ratio that agrees, would move the year number from a single test to a stable verdict.

approaches.note: A 10^5 stratified permutation on experimental GO and HPO annotations is an INDRA query the server can run, unless pleiotropy, publication count and expression breadth are so collinear that strata are empty.
IMPC statistical results are public, but the behavioural pipeline measures activity and anxiety, so the learning endpoint is likely to be restated as a broader proxy.
Network separation on indra_rel edges is a Cypher export plus a degree-matched null, and the stated risk is that separation tracks publication count rather than shared machinery.
A propensity-matched overlap in human and mouse is the same ontology test with a harder balance diagnostic, which can fail leave-one-term-out even when the odds ratio is large.
Holding out papers that mention both domains is the right leakage control, and the slice already says INDRA coverage and direction are uneven, so five hubs can dominate the excess.
The odds-ratio permutation with IEA excluded, and the same threshold on GO:0005216 and GO:0005921, is the acceptance test in executable form and should return a number rather than a plan.

Counting INDRA statements of evidence at least 5 across the cut is a second query on the same sets, and a null count is a definite 'not wired' result only if the degree-preserving draws are actually balanced.
Stopping when QuickGO has no assignment dates is an allowed completion, and that stop is likely enough that the pre-2015 odds ratio often never gets computed.

problems.rationale: Acceptance requires a model that maps published Vmem images of perturbed and control embryos or fragments to anatomical class at a pre-registered accuracy on held-out images, with the train and test papers named. The only public material in the slice is figures in a few open papers and BETSE defaults, not specimen-linked raw stacks, and thirteen related Levin tests are already waiting on data. Leave-one-paper-out on captions is the least impossible route and is likely to stop under 20 independent experiments or at the majority class; a penetrance meta-analysis can finish without being that decoder, so I do not use its product as a floor. frontier_simulate is a bounded preview and is not evidence. Individual-level DiBAC images with outcomes would move me, and this swarm cannot generate them, which is why the year increment is small.

approaches.note: Harvesting open-licence dye figures is possible, but most images are group representatives without individual outcomes, and fewer than five studies per tissue makes leave-one-study-out inconclusive.
Ten held-out perturbations with known molecular targets and channel densities are not in the published parameter sets, and a frontier preview cannot substitute for a calibrated BETSE run.
Double-extracting penetrance against a Vmem shift is literature work inside the tractable band, but fewer than 15 joint reports or a significant Egger bias leaves the slope uninterpretable.
Two hundred specimen-linked raw maps and thirty per held-out class are the sample the slice says may not be public, so chance-on-holdout is not even reachable.
Fitting conductances on one perturbation and predicting three unseen intervention classes needs quantitative coupling on the same specimens, which the proposer correctly marks as a long shot.
Three named papers and a dipole-plus-domain feature set are concrete, and the approach expects to be underpowered below 20 independent experiments rather than to clear accuracy 0.7.
Pinning Pietak and Levin 2016 defaults and scoring two pre-named perturbations is a small BETSE job if the engine runs, and either misclassification is a definite failure of that frozen model.
The identifiability lemma for dipole and domain count is a short Lean proof, but figure measurements are often too coarse for the 0.1 tolerance, which stops the empirical half.

problems.rationale: The acceptance test is a re-run of the Biswas protocol on the original 35 BioModels and at least 350 random ODEs matched on node count, edge density, kinetic form and parameter ranges, with code and seeds logged. RoadRunner-style simulation is in scope and BioModels are open, but the comparison is meaningless until the implementation recovers the paper's memory calls, and the slice warns that protocol details may be underspecified. Topology-versus-parameter surgery and motif sweeps use the same probes, so they do not add an independent chance if reproduction fails. An executable probe that agrees on at least 90 percent of the original calls would move the 30-day number sharply; CRNT will not, because many of the 35 models are not mass-action.

approaches.note: Three hundred and fifty matched networks is a finite ensemble, but agreement below 90 percent with the published calls invalidates the ratio even after the runs finish.

I put completion at the bottom of the tractable band because twenty variants times three surgeries is large, and discarding unstable SBML variants can leave a biased subset whose retention rates do not mean anything.
The linear-stability lemma is a reasonable Lean fragment, but CRNT covers only the mass-action subset and memory inside the test window can be a transient the classification rules out.
I sit just under the tractable band because 3500 convergent nulls is an order of magnitude more simulation than the acceptance minimum, and the same 80 percent reproduction gate can abort it.
Ten thousand parameter sets per signed motif is an expensive enumeration, and memory that depends on diffuse parameters leaves no motif with a stable 0.25 effect.

I rate completion above the hard label because failing to reproduce the paper's count on the original 35 models is a defined early stop, while a real enrichment call still needs that reproduction to hold.
Arms that rewire topology or redraw parameters are the same probes with a pre-registered four-way call, and they are wasted if arm C does not match the first null on the same seeds.

Existence of habituation on an open set of a three-variable negative-feedback system, and impossibility for linear kinetics, is a fiddly ODE proof that would not answer whether BioModels are enriched.

problems.rationale: Acceptance needs a quantitative prediction derived from a generative model fixed before the data, plus a pre-registered comparison to published planarian or Xenopus regeneration time courses. A finite complete-class theorem can show that a free target is tautological, which is real progress on the falsifier, but it does not supply the empirical half, so that product is not a floor under the problem. The data routes need regeneration times for four or more fragment classes, and the slice says those series are sparse, old, or cartoons; a Kuchling lattice stops if the paper has no numerical parameter set. One table of times against fragment class, with the 2015 target's free parameters enumerated so the ranking cannot be flipped after the fact, would move me.

approaches.note: A finite complete-class construction on Finset policies is the kind of theorem Lean can finish, but expected free energy has several definitions and the result may have to be stated per definition.

Reimplementing Friston et al. 2015 and freezing an excision envelope is possible, yet the envelope over stated parameter ranges can contain every monotone recovery curve and then no observation refutes it.

Picasso-tadpole organ positions live in figures with few stages, and a negative slope of correction on displacement is shared with non-inferential gradient models, so it would not isolate active inference.
Specimen-level regeneration times with quantified initial surprise are the missing public table, and retargeting the morphology after each perturbation is the failure the problem is trying to forbid.

I put completion under the tractable band because a thousand datasets from three generators, each fit with simulation-based calibration, is more than a 30-day preview, though low specificity would itself be a decisive negative.
A Spearman rank above 0.5 on four fragment classes is a sharp test, and the approach stops as inconclusive when the papers show only unlabeled cartoons.
The free-target tautology is the easier lemma; the fixed 2015 ranking is decisive only if no leftover parameter flips it, which is the harder half of the same module.
The lattice update runs only if Kuchling et al. 2020 states a complete numerical parameter set, and a schematic model is a failed start rather than a polarity prediction.
